clue.text: Charity makes radical angry

parts.note: a red is a political radical, a left-winger
cross means annoyed or angry

explanation.surface: A charity's work stirs a firebrand to fury.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'makes' as 'causes to be', but the two adjectives are simply placed side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: The Red Cross is the famous international humanitarian organisation that helps victims of war and disaster.

clue.text: Artist holding stick in country

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it inside, so the artist's letters enclose the stick

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist
a wand is a thin stick

explanation.surface: A painter carries a walking stick through a foreign land.
explanation.definitionFit: Rwanda is a small landlocked nation in central-east Africa, so it is a country.

clue.text: Walked northwards to conceal beginning of moonlight flit

indicators.note: in a down clue going north means reading upwards, so the word is written backwards
concealing something hides it inside, so the reversed word wraps round the single letter

parts.note: paced means walked steadily

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is just its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of moonlight

explanation.surface: Someone sneaks off in the night, moving north to hide their escape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moonlight flit' looks like one phrase, but it splits: 'moonlight' feeds the wordplay and 'flit' is the definition. A moonlight flit is fleeing secretly at night to dodge debts.
explanation.definitionFit: To decamp is to leave suddenly or secretly, which is what flitting means in British usage.

clue.text: Irritating engineer capturing violinist's heart

indicators.note: capturing means holding the other piece inside

parts.note: to engineer something is to rig it, arrange it underhandedly
the heart of violinist is its central three letters

explanation.surface: An irritable engineer makes off with the essence of a violinist's performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engineer' looks like a person but is the verb meaning rig; RIG is 'capturing' LIN, the central letters of 'violinist'.
explanation.definitionFit: Riling means annoying or angering someone, so it is a synonym of irritating.

clue.text: Party's commercial somehow led to seat for woman

parts.note: a side is a party in a dispute, so party's gives side's
an ad is a commercial

indicators.note: somehow means in some way or other, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A political party's advert somehow ended up with a woman being given a seat.
explanation.walkthrough: SIDES and AD, then LED rearranged to DLE. 'Party' looks political, but it is one side of a dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: A side-saddle is a saddle on which the rider sits with both legs on one side, traditionally used by women.

clue.text: Sailor brewing tea before head of steam dies down

indicators.note: before means the brewed letters come ahead of the next piece

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

indicators.note: brewing means being made, so the letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of steam

explanation.surface: A sailor's tea is brewing until the steam dies away.
explanation.walkthrough: AB, then TEA 'brewing' into ATE, then S, the 'head of steam'.
explanation.definitionFit: To abate is to lessen or subside, as a storm does when it dies down.

clue.text: Declared support for a strike breaker bringing card game

indicators.note: something declared is spoken out, so the answer matches the sound of the words that follow

parts.note: to support is to back, and a rat is a worker who breaks a strike

explanation.surface: Publicly endorsing a scab leads to a game of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Baccarat is a casino card game in which players bet on which hand comes closest to nine.

clue.text: Bear moving into wood for short refreshment stop

indicators.note: going into something means being placed inside it

parts.note: teak is a hardwood

indicators.note: letters that are moving shift their positions into a new order

parts.note: the four letters shuffled

explanation.surface: A bear lumbers into the forest for a quick snack.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea break is a short pause from work for a cup of tea and a bite to eat.

clue.text: Set out on popular route with instrument

indicators.note: on means the next pieces follow on after the rearranged letters
out means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written
in means fashionable, popular
a way is a route

explanation.surface: Someone sets off on a well-trodden path carrying a musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: SET 'out' gives STE, then IN and WAY. 'Set out' reads as starting a journey, but 'out' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Steinway is the famous make of piano, so a Steinway is the instrument itself.

clue.text: A drug company associated with dodgy deal gets award

indicators.note: associated with means the company is joined to what follows

parts.note: C is short for cocaine, a drug

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A pharmaceutical company mixed up in a shady deal somehow wins an award.
explanation.walkthrough: A, C and CO, then DEAL made 'dodgy' into LADE.
explanation.definitionFit: An accolade is an honour or prize given in recognition of merit.

clue.text: Concoct a verse containing a series of notes

indicators.note: the phrase before holds the answer inside it, spanning its word breaks

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, the whole second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: An instruction to a songwriter to compose some lines that cover a run of musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: An octave is the span of eight notes of a scale, from one note to the next of the same name.

clue.text: Get smaller car in vessel

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another means it is placed within the second word's letters

parts.note: a dish is a shallow vessel for food
the Mini is the classic small British car

explanation.surface: A little car loaded onto a ship, as if to shrink it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a boat, but here it is a serving bowl.
explanation.definitionFit: To diminish is to become less or reduce in size, an exact verb synonym for shrinking.

clue.text: Bird circling a run in rabbits' home

indicators.note: circling means going round, so the bird holds the other letters

parts.note: the wren is a small bird
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A bird circles a run where rabbits live.
explanation.definitionFit: A warren is a network of burrows where rabbits live together.

clue.text: Choose a flower said to be in veggie condiment

indicators.note: what is said is spoken aloud, so the answer is the sound of the phrase before

parts.note: to choose is to pick, and the lily is a flower

explanation.surface: Selecting a bloom to garnish a vegetable relish.
explanation.definitionFit: Piccalilli is a bright yellow British pickle of chopped vegetables in a mustard sauce.

clue.text: Join savings scheme used by graduates in African capital

parts.note: to add is to join on
an ISA is a British individual savings account, a tax-free savings scheme
two BAs, Bachelors of Arts

explanation.surface: Advice to sign up for a savings plan popular with university leavers in an African city.
explanation.definitionFit: Addis Ababa is the capital city of Ethiopia, in the Horn of Africa.

clue.text: See trio playing Chopin's prelude in secret

indicators.note: musicians playing a piece perform it, and here the letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written for the shuffle

indicators.note: a prelude comes at the start, so only the composer's first letter is used

parts.note: the opening letter of Chopin

explanation.surface: An invitation to watch a chamber group performing a short piano piece in private.
explanation.walkthrough: Chopin wrote famous preludes, so 'Chopin's prelude' looks like a piece of music.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric means understood only by a select few initiates, close in sense to hidden or secret.

clue.text: In March, island is a heaven on earth

indicators.note: placing one thing in another puts its letters inside the second word

parts.note: to parade is to march in procession
Is. is the map abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A spring holiday on an island feels like heaven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'March' looks like the month, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Paradise is an idyllic place of perfect happiness, which is what a heaven on earth describes.

clue.text: Second fiddle eating centre of onion is more malodorous

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second

indicators.note: something eaten goes inside the eater, so these letters wrap round the next piece

parts.note: to tinker is to fiddle about with something

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letter alone

parts.note: the middle letter of onion

explanation.surface: The second violinist munching an onion smells worse than ever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second fiddle' looks like one phrase for a supporting player; split it into an abbreviation and a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Stinkier means smelling worse, the comparative of stinky, which matches more foul-smelling.

clue.text: Wise guy in fishing boat interrupted by skipper's last story

indicators.note: being interrupted means having something break into the middle, so the boat's letters are split around the rest

parts.note: a smack is a single-masted fishing boat

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter alone

parts.note: the final letter of skipper
a tale is a story

explanation.surface: A know-it-all aboard a trawler is cut off mid-yarn by the captain.
explanation.definitionFit: A smart aleck is an irritatingly cocky know-it-all, just as 'wise guy' sarcastically labels one.

clue.text: Like ruler to be demanding

parts.note: as means like, in the manner of
a king is a ruler

explanation.surface: Behaving like a monarch means making constant demands.
explanation.definitionFit: Asking means requesting or requiring, so it substitutes for demanding as a participle.

clue.text: Clergyman with parking offence

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
arson, deliberately setting fire to property, is a criminal offence

explanation.surface: A vicar has been caught committing a parking offence.
explanation.definitionFit: A parson is a parish priest or vicar, a member of the clergy.

clue.text: One not to be trusted with artist's equipment

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for with
an easel is the stand a painter rests a canvas on

explanation.surface: A shifty character carrying a painter's kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' looks like a link word but supplies the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A weasel is figuratively a sly, deceitful person, someone too treacherous to rely on.

clue.text: Attempt to steal woman's radio

indicators.note: stealing means taking something in and holding it, so the attempt's letters close round the woman

parts.note: a try is an attempt
Ann is a common woman's name

explanation.surface: Someone tries to make off with a lady's wireless.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'woman's' is read as 'woman has' joining to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tranny was dated British slang for a transistor radio, the portable set popular in the 1960s.

clue.text: German ladies confused about second movement in ballet

indicators.note: confused things are muddled, so the letters of the word before are jumbled

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for German

indicators.note: about means around, so the jumbled letters go round the next piece

parts.note: the six letters rearranged
S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: German women baffled by a second section of a ballet.
explanation.definitionFit: A glissade is a gliding step in classical ballet, one foot sliding out and the other following.

clue.text: Extolling the virtues of peeled fruit

indicators.note: a peeled word has lost its outer layer, the first and last letters

parts.note: praising is extolling the virtues of something
the outer letters of praising, the ones removed

explanation.surface: Someone sings the praises of a piece of fruit that has had its skin taken off.
explanation.walkthrough: PRAISING is 'peeled' of its first and last letters. 'peeled fruit' reads as one phrase, but 'peeled' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A raisin is a dried grape, eaten as a fruit in its own right.

clue.text: I spell out one, primarily syntactical, way to indicate missing text

indicators.note: letters spelt out of order are set out in a fresh arrangement

parts.note: the six letters reworked
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter is wanted

parts.note: the opening letter of syntactical

explanation.surface: A grammarian describes setting out the punctuation that marks an omission.
explanation.definitionFit: An ellipsis is the row of three dots showing that words have been left out of a quotation.

clue.text: After church, rector enters retired bishop's office for toast

indicators.note: coming after means the following letters are placed behind the opening abbreviation

parts.note: CH is the abbreviation for church

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the office is read backwards
to enter is to go inside, so the clergyman's letter is put within the office

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese or seat of office
R is the abbreviation for rector

explanation.surface: After the service the vicar visits a retired bishop to raise a glass.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheers is the drinking salutation said as glasses are raised, exactly what a toast is.

clue.text: Pure spirit drunk by tipsy rival

indicators.note: drunk by means swallowed, so the spirit goes inside the other letters
tipsy means unsteady from drink, so these letters reel into a new order

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: A competitor, already merry, downs a neat measure of spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk by' sits naturally in the drinking picture, but it tells you the spirit goes inside the jumbled competitor, which is VIRAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Virginal means chaste and untouched, which is one sense of pure.
